APPROVE substantive target SHA-256 9abc51b03eb73b5be4f3d65dbb94aab0661f1df8b9626850a2d204d73c4e2ef4, 292 lines, whitespace check clean.

I rescanned the full document and the semantic delta against the pinned primary records. The narrowed key boundary.pyscenedetect.content now matches the only nominated implementation. Scientific role is explicitly a nonempty set; ContentDetector separately emits raw Measurement metrics and derived Proposal candidates, and the non-conflation rule prevents measurement authority from laundering a proposal into an observation or acceptance. Emitted boundary proposals now avoids collision with the resolver-owned Accepted disposition. The registry, leaf record, first-court scope, and completion gate agree on that boundary.

Primary evidence remains consistent: the official FFmpeg record identifies 9.0.1 Lei and its 2026-08-12 release; the pinned configure file supports the recorded GPL/version3/nonfree, network, component, and ffprobe switches; PyPI records both 0.7.1 artifact hashes and trusted-publishing provenance bound to commit 6ebb72392de8acfb6c539bf15d0aa912ce7ab6b2; the pinned ContentDetector implementation exposes the documented weighted metrics and process_frame proposals; and the OpenCV wheel notice confirms why native-library and notice closure must remain held.

The new cache/CI, notice, output-retention, candidate-family, and authority wording remains fail-closed. I find no substantive blocker to the documentation-only component-ledger leg. This approval does not authorize source media, packages, containers, codecs, models, terms, builds, execution, B0/P1/C1 closure, or any accepted narrative boundary. I will perform the requested final artifact-hash rescan after the durable review-record-only append.
